nodes.name: NiFe PBA co-precipitation
nodes.procedure: 0.264 g of potassium hexacyanoferrate(III) was dissolved in 60 mL DI water to form solution A. 0.348 g of nickel(II) nitrate hexahydrate and 0.441 g of trisodium citrate dihydrate were dissolved into 40 mL DI water to form solution B. Then, solution A was added to solution B under vigorous stirring for 24 h. After stirring for 24 h, the co-precipitation was obtained by centrifugation, washed with DI water, and dried in a drying oven overnight at 70°C.

nodes.name: F-NiFe PBA hydrothermal fluorination
nodes.procedure: 0.01 M NH4F was mixed with 0.40 g of coprecipitation of NiFe PBA in 40 mL DI water and sonicated for 15 min. Then, the resultant solution was put into a 100 mL autoclave with Teflon-lined for 2 h at 150°C via hydrothermal treatment. Next, the product was obtained by centrifugation, washed with DI water, and dried in a drying oven for 6 h at 70°C. The best result was obtained from F-NiFe PBA with 0.01 M of NH4F.

nodes.name: GQD hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: A 0.40 g of citric acid was added to 40 mL DI water and sonicated for 30 min. Next, the solution was put into a 100 mL autoclave with Teflon-lined for 3 h at 200°C. After the hydrothermal treatment, the clear solution was dialyzed with DI water for 20 min using a dialysis tube (Spectrum Lab, Inc, 3000 Da) to separate it from the impurities.

nodes.name: GQD/F-NiFe PBA tandem assembly
nodes.procedure: 0.05 M NH4F mixed with 0.40 g of co-precipitation of NiFe PBA in 40 mL DI water and sonicated for 15 min. Then, the resultant solution was put into a 100 mL autoclave with Teflon-lined for 2 h at 150°C via hydrothermal treatment. After hydrothermal treatment, cool to room temperature. Next, 1 mL of GQD solution was added into the F-NiFe PBA solution and mixed under vigorous stirring for 2 h at room temperature. The final product was centrifuged, washed with DI water, and dried in an oven for 6 h at 70°C. The best result was obtained from GQD/F-NiFe PBA with 0.05 M of NH4F and 1 mL of GQD concentration.

nodes.description: OER performance screening of F-NiFe PBA variants in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: Fig. 2a demonstrates the effect of fluorine doping concentration for F-NiFe PBA on the electrochemical OER performance using the LSV curve. The 0.01F-NiFe PBA catalyst exhibits an OER overpotential of 362 mV at the current density of 50 mA cm−2 in 1.0 M KOH, which is slightly lower than those of 0.03F-NiFe PBA (376 mV), 0.05F-NiFe PBA (379 mV), 0.1 F-NiFe PBA (400 mV), and the pristine NiFe PBA (423 mV). However, the electrocatalytic performance of 0.2 F-NiFe PBA (445 mV) was poor... the corresponding Tafel slope of 0.01F-NiFe PBA is 60.26 mV dec−1, lower than that of NiFe PBA (144.23 mV dec−1).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe PBA shows smooth nanocubes surface with average particle size ~150 nm; F-NiFe PBA shows irregular morphology transformation due to hydrothermal process.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of the NiFe PBA was investigated by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) as revealed in Fig. 1a. The morphology of NiFe PBA shows a smooth nanocubes surface with an average particle size is about 150 nm. Meanwhile, the fluorine-doping on NiFe PBA (F-NiFe PBA) induced the transformation of the NiFe PBA cubical shape into irregular due to the hydrothermal process (Fig. 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Prominent diffraction peaks slightly broadened after fluorination at 17.0° and 25.0° indicating F⁺ ionic exchange interaction with Ni₃(Fe(CN)₆)₂ characteristic peaks (JCPDS 86-0501); peak intensity decreases with GQD concentration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystallographic structure was confirmed by X-ray diffraction powder (XRD), and the prominent diffraction peaks after fluorination were slightly broadened on F-NiFe PBA. The broadened peaks appear at 17.0° and 25.0° after fluorine doping... the XRD patterns reveal that after the GQD was added to the F-NiFe PBA, the main characteristic peaks remained in the NiFe PBA peaks.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe PBA shows Ni 8.3 at% and Fe 6.46 at%; F-NiFe PBA shows decreased Ni 7.6 at% and Fe 5.23 at%; GQD/F-NiFe PBA shows homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, F, O.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The metal composition of pristine NiFe PBA (Ni and Fe) was 8.3 and 6.46 (at. %) before fluorine doping, which is much higher than 7.6 and 5.23 (at. %) after fluorine doping... The EDX elemental mapping of the relevant GQD/F-NiFe PBA indicates that all elements Ni, Fe, F, and O are homogeneously distributed.

nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice spacing of 0.539 nm and 0.292 nm (shown in Figure S2) could be well aligned to the (200) and (400) crystallography plane of the cubic NiFe PBA structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows Ni oxidation state increase from Ni²⁺ to Ni³⁺ after GQD integration into F-NiFe PBA; Ni-O bond length 1.56 Å → 1.60 Å (F-doped) → 1.64 Å (GQD); Ni-Ni 2.46 Å → 2.51 Å → 2.56 Å indicating Ni-F bonding; Fe K-edge shows no apparent changes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Through the Ni K-edge XANES spectra... the oxidation state of Ni rises from Ni²⁺ ions to higher valence states, which refers to Ni³⁺. The NiFe PBA inner shell displayed an average bond length of Ni-O of 1.56 Å. Following the introduction of F-doped to NiFe PBA and the integration of GQD into F-NiFe PBA... shift to the longer distance by 1.60 Å and rise to 1.64 Å... While the average Ni-Ni bond was 2.46 Å, both the F-doped and GQDs-modified F-NiFe PBA showed longer Ni-Ni bonds, to 2.51 Å and 2.56 Å.
